subject: Hospitality
title: Loyalty Programs: Golden Handcuffs
description: A quick, practical guide to Loyalty Programs: Golden Handcuffs.

hook.text: Hotel loyalty programs now have more members than most countries have citizens. Marriott Bonvoy alone has 200+ million.

buildup.text: Points, status tiers, free upgrades, late checkout—loyalty programs reward repeat guests with escalating perks.

discovery.text: The real purpose isn't rewarding loyalty—it's creating switching costs. Once you have status, leaving feels like losing.

twist.text: Loyalty points are a billion-dollar currency. Hotels sell points to credit card companies for more than they earn from rooms.

climax.text: Points programs have become financial products. Some analysts say Marriott's loyalty program is worth more than its hotels.

punchline.text: Not rewards—retention. Loyalty programs are elegant traps.

quiz.question: Why are hotel loyalty programs so valuable to the business?
options: They create switching costs and generate billions from point sales to credit card companies
